root_cause.text: The `addrs_lock` spinlock protecting address list updates was incorrectly scoped to individual `ipvlan` devices instead of the shared `ipvlan` port, failing to serialize concurrent address modifications across multiple devices on the same port when IPv6 events occur outside the RTNL lock.

relevance_review.reason: The vulnerability root cause involves the addrs_lock spinlock being incorrectly scoped at the device level instead of the port level. This group's intent to remove the addrs_lock from ipvl_dev directly addresses this locking issue, indicating the vulnerability has been fixed through an alternative synchronization mechanism where the lock is no longer needed.
The group contains no code changes or intent description. Without modifications to the addrs_lock scoping or ipvlan port/device synchronization logic, it cannot address the vulnerability.

The group explicitly corrects the spinlock target from device-level to port-level and adds protection against race conditions in IPv6 address handling, which directly addresses the incorrect scoping and serialization issues described in the root cause.

The code changes directly address the root cause by shifting the addrs_lock scope from the individual ipvlan device to the shared ipvlan port, ensuring proper serialization of concurrent address modifications across devices on the same port.
